adb_wireless.title: Pair Wireless debugging
adb_wireless.description: On {name} open Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, then enter the port and code shown.

data_description.connect_port: Port next to the IP address on the main Wireless debugging screen (e.g. 44491). Leave blank to discover it automatically.
data_description.pairing_port: Port shown in the Pair device with pairing code dialog (e.g. 41745).

data_description.keepalive_interval: How often to check the ADB connection and refresh HDMI / now-playing state.

adb_offline_tls.title: {name}: HDMI control offline
adb_offline_tls.description:
Home Assistant can't reach {name} over Wireless debugging, so HDMI inputs can't be discovered or switched.

1. Make sure the TV is on and Developer options → Wireless debugging is enabled.
2. If the TV was reset or debugging authorizations were revoked, re-pair from the integration options (Pair Wireless debugging).

The connection port is discovered automatically. This issue clears on its own once ADB reconnects.

Last error: {error}

adb_offline_classic.title: {name}: HDMI control offline
adb_offline_classic.description:
Home Assistant can't reach {name} over ADB on port {port}, so HDMI inputs can't be discovered or switched.

1. On the TV open Developer options and turn on Network debugging.
2. Accept the Allow debugging prompt on the TV (choose Always allow).

This issue clears on its own once ADB reconnects.

Last error: {error}
